2123719751503315383.author: zenkaixbt
2123719751503315383.context: zenkaixbt: el próximo halving es en 507 días; afirma que 'históricamente siempre funcionó' comprar BTC 500 días antes del halving y vender 500 días después. Post de hace ~20 min con 35 likes y 24 respuestas.
2123719751503315383.suggested_text:
Four halvings is a small sample, and "always" carries a lot of weight in that sentence. The mechanism behind it is real, though: the next halving cuts the block subsidy from 3.125 to 1.5625 BTC, so new supply drops from ~450 to ~225 BTC a day, and by then only 3.125% of the 21M will be left to issue.

What changed is who sits on the other side of that trade. In 2012 and 2016, miner selling was a big share of daily flow; today spot ETFs and corporate treasuries can absorb or dump several days' worth of issuance in a single session. The supply shock shrinks every cycle in absolute terms, while demand gets harder to read.

The calendar still matters. Maybe just not in the way a 500-day rule assumes.

2123724492396794150.author: WuBlockchain
2123724492396794150.context: WuBlockchain: Ledger confirma hardware wallets alteradas físicamente (ataque a la cadena de suministro) en Berlín; dos equipos sospechosos en Dubái siguen en investigación. Noticia fresca de custodia con 24 likes y solo 16 respuestas, sin respuesta de @ForecastQuant.
2123724492396794150.suggested_text:
The uncomfortable part of this story isn't Ledger specifically. It's that "bought from an authorized retailer" is no longer a guarantee. A supply-chain attack doesn't need to break the secure element; it only needs to sit between the factory and you long enough to modify the hardware or plant a seed you didn't generate.

That's why the setup ritual matters more than the brand: create the seed yourself on the device, never accept a pre-printed one, run the genuine/attestation check, and test a recovery before sending real funds. Keeping the signing device air-gapped adds another layer, because a compromised unit with no path to the network has a much harder time leaking anything.

Most of these losses are decided in the first minutes of setup, not years later. Few people treat those minutes as the part that actually matters.

Post en español de hace ~46 min con 9 likes, 4 guardados y 1 respuesta.
2123764023866839146.suggested_text:
Buena imagen la del mapa. El miedo a la autocustodia casi nunca es a la tecnología. Es a no saber qué pasa si algo falla, y eso se resuelve entendiendo tres piezas: qué es realmente la semilla (las llaves, no una contraseña), dónde se genera y cómo se recupera sin el dispositivo original.

Lo que más confianza da es ensayar la pérdida antes de que ocurra: crear la semilla uno mismo, mandar un monto chico, borrar el equipo y recuperar los fondos desde cero. El que hizo ese ejercicio una vez ya no depende de que algo «funcione»; sabe por qué funciona.

Y esta semana sumó un matiz: Ledger confirmó equipos alterados físicamente en Berlín. El riesgo se está corriendo hacia el momento de la configuración, justo la parte del mapa que casi nadie mira con calma.

2123780581414825992.author: Cryptollica
2123780581414825992.context: Cryptollica: la cantidad de BTC mantenida en pérdida acaba de marcar un máximo histórico; lo llama la señal de piso más fuerte de la historia de Bitcoin y una oportunidad de compra generacional (con gráfico).
2123780581414825992.suggested_text:
What this metric really measures is pressure. Every coin held at a loss is someone whose cost basis sits above today's price, and each of them faces the same choice: sell into weakness or wait it out. Historically, bottoms have formed when enough of those coins changed hands, moving from underwater holders to buyers with a much lower cost basis.

There's a nuance with an all-time high in absolute terms, though. A big part of this cycle's supply was bought in the ETF era at six-figure prices, so with BTC near $61K-62K a record amount underwater is partly arithmetic. The percentage of supply at a loss, and how fast it's being redistributed, says more than the raw number.

Pain this concentrated tends to resolve one of two ways. Which one usually shows up in who is still holding six months later.

The protocol side of this is simple: issuance is fixed in code. At the next halving only 3.125% of the 21M will be left to mine, and the subsidy drops from 3.125 to 1.5625 BTC per block, from roughly 450 to 225 BTC a day: https://x.com/ForecastQuant/status/2122747344701501622

Paper claims can't touch that schedule. What they can change is the effective float that price discovery sees, for as long as buyers accept an IOU instead of coins they control. 2123870827976196235.author: cointradernik
2123870827976196235.context: Nik (en inglés, con gráfico): dice que Bitcoin acaba de hacer historia con el precio más bajo de siempre en relación con su power law "cruda" y con su power law ajustada por volatilidad, superando el 24 de agosto de 2015. Worth remembering what a power law fit actually is: a straight line through log price vs. log time, fitted on past data. When $BTC prints its lowest ratio ever against it, two readings are possible, and they aren't mutually exclusive: either price is deeply discounted, or the slope itself is flattening as the asset matures.

History gives both sides ammunition. On the original 2013 power law from Dacoinminster, the 2017 top reached 9.4x the curve while the 2018 low already slipped below it. The band around the line has always been wide in both directions, which is why a single extreme reading says more about positioning than about timing.

The real question a record undershoot raises isn't only "is it cheap?" but whether an exponent fitted on the early years still describes a trillion-dollar asset.

2123880466453573694.author: Sykodelic_
2123880466453573694.context: Sykodelic (con gráfico): Bitcoin marcó un nuevo mínimo hoy y este ya empata como el mercado bajista más largo de la historia junto con 2015, pero con una caída mucho menor: en 2015, a esta altura, BTC caía 86%; hoy cae 54%. 2123880466453573694.suggested_text:
Depth and duration usually move together, which is what makes this one so unusual. In the cycles I track, the 2011 bear took BTC down 92.7% and needed 622 days to reclaim the high; the 2013 cycle bottomed at -84.5% and took 1,177 days. A 54% drawdown stretched over this long looks less like a capitulation and more like a slow grind, with supply changing hands instead of being dumped all at once.

The trade-off is that a shallow drawdown spares holders the worst, but it also leaves behind more of the forced selling that deep crashes usually flush out in one go. When price doesn't do the cleaning, time usually has to.

Whether that job is already done, or whether time is still doing what price hasn't, is the part no chart answers on its own.

2123889524283674898.author: Strategy
2123889524283674898.context: Strategy ($MSTR): en el mercado bajista de 2022 su Net Reserve era negativa y un tercio de sus BTC estaba pignorado como colateral, pero sobrevivieron. Hoy dicen tener una Net Reserve de US$35.000 millones, todos sus BTC libres de gravámenes, y más convicción y opcionalidad que nunca.
2123889524283674898.suggested_text:
Pledged vs unencumbered is the detail most people skip, and it's the one that decides who makes it through a drawdown. In 2022 BTC fell roughly 77% from its high; coins posted as collateral in a move like that stop being an asset you hold and become a margin call someone else controls.

Past cycles put the stakes in numbers: after the 2013 peak BTC dropped 84.5% and took 1,177 days to reclaim it, and the 2011 cycle needed 622 days after a 92.7% fall. Anyone forced to sell inside those windows never saw the recovery, no matter how right they were about the long term: https://x.com/ForecastQuant/status/2122375393776951738

Unencumbered coins buy time, and time is what a bear market really tests. The harder question for any balance sheet is what happens when "temporary" lasts longer than the plan assumed.

2123889918988726699.author: Sykodelic_
2123889918988726699.context: Sykodelic (73,5K seguidores), citando a un trader agotado por el año: dice que han sido los 14 meses más duros que ha visto en cripto, 'el ciclo bajista más largo con la caída más corta', y que en octubre de 2025 solo Bitcoin hizo nuevos máximos mientras el resto no se expandió.
2123889918988726699.suggested_text:
Shallow drawdown, long duration: that combination is often harder on people than a sharp crash, because there's no capitulation moment to anchor to, just months of grind. Past cycles had the opposite shape: after the 2011 peak BTC fell 92.7% and needed 622 days to reclaim it; after 2013 it dropped 84.5% and took 1,177 days.

Depth hurts once. Time wears conviction down slowly, and most people who leave a cycle don't sell into the crash, they sell somewhere in the middle of the boredom.

If drawdowns keep getting shallower as the asset matures, the more interesting question is whether the recovery clock stretches in the opposite direction.

2123890451241468022.author: Mattertrades
2123890451241468022.context: Matter (en inglés): analiza el hackeo de $6.400M a Binance. Binance cubrió a los clientes con ~$5.000M de activos propios, así que casi no hubo compras en el mercado y el BTC robado sigue en manos del atacante. Su tesis es que tras el hackeo los desks bajaron sus saldos en exchanges, hubo menos liquidez para absorber liquidaciones y por eso un problema de custodia sigue apareciendo en el gráfico de BTC (~$2,71T a ~$2,15T de capitalización cripto). Cuenta mediana, post de hace ~30 min con 5 guardados y 1 respuesta.
2123890451241468022.suggested_text:
The part that gets lost in "customers were made whole" is what that guarantee actually is: a claim on the exchange's balance sheet, not a key you hold. It worked this time because Binance had roughly $5B of the exact assets on hand. And the mechanism you describe cuts both ways: when desks pull size off exchanges after a hack, liquidity thins for everyone, but whoever already held $BTC in self-custody was never in the queue waiting to be covered.

A treasury can replace coins one for one. What it can't replace is the assumption that the coins were ever yours while they sat there.

2123957640950677877.author: fluffycrypt
2123957640950677877.context: Fluffy (157K seguidores), con un video de 46 s: "Este millonario cripto filtró la frase semilla de su wallet durante un livestream. Sus espectadores le robaron $2,5M en segundos". La cifra y el caso son lo que afirma el post; no están verificados.
2123957640950677877.suggested_text:
A seed phrase isn't a password you can reset; it is the wallet. Whoever sees those 12 or 24 words has exactly the same authority as the owner, and a sweep script can move everything before anyone realizes what happened. No support line, no chargeback.

That's why the core rule of self-custody is that the words never touch anything with a camera, a screen or an internet connection: not a photo, not a notes app, not a stream. A hardware wallet protects the signing, but it can't protect a phrase that has already been shown.

Most losses like this aren't a failure of Bitcoin's cryptography. They're a failure of the few seconds when the secret leaves the paper.

2124183498223129066.suggested_text:
Two sources, and the mix between them is the real story: newly issued coins plus transaction fees. Today the larger share typically comes from issuance, 3.125 BTC per block, roughly 450 BTC a day.

That subsidy halves every 210,000 blocks. At the next halving it drops to 1.5625 BTC, about 225 a day, and only 3.125% of the 21M will be left to issue. Every cut shifts more of the security budget onto fees, meaning onto the people actually using the chain.

The long-run question isn't whether miners get paid. It's whether demand for blockspace grows fast enough to replace a subsidy that keeps halving toward zero.

Talvez a parte mais interessante dessa história não seja o dia 21, e sim o que aconteceu com quem estava no mercado nos meses ao redor dele.

2124265359192539159.author: 3orovik
2124265359192539159.context: @3orovik (borovik, 222.220 seguidores): "We're in the longest Bitcoin bear market in history. But guess what, I AM BULLISH!!" Post de ~2 h con 139 likes, 33 respuestas y 4.138 vistas, con mucha conversación. Ángulo: caídas y tiempo de recuperación entre ciclos.
2124265359192539159.suggested_text:
Long bear markets feel endless from the inside, but the recovery side of the history is just as uneven. After the 2011 peak, Bitcoin fell 92.7% and took 622 days to get back to the high. After 2013 it dropped 84.5% and needed 1,177 days, almost twice as long, from a smaller loss.

So the duration of a drawdown never told you much about how deep it was, or when it would end. What changed between those cycles was who was holding through them, and how much of the supply stopped moving.

Being bullish in a long bear isn't really a contradiction. It's mostly a bet on time rather than on price, and that's a bet the calendar rarely settles when people expect it to.

Solid checklist, and "don't trust, verify" is the right instinct. It's worth being precise about what Proof of Reserves verifies, though: it's a snapshot showing the exchange held assets against the customer balances included at that moment. It says little about what happens between snapshots, and it doesn't change the fact that coins on an exchange are a claim on the exchange, not coins you control.

Cold storage, multi-approval transfers and an emergency fund lower the risk of a hack. They don't remove counterparty risk: paused withdrawals, frozen accounts, insolvency. For coins you plan to hold for years, the strongest form of "verify" is holding the keys yourself, ideally on a device that never touches the internet. 2124854961372615039.suggested_text:
That distinction matters more than it looks. A power law in time describes the price trend; it doesn't explain it. Time is really standing in for other variables, like adoption, hash rate and liquidity, each growing on its own curve.

It also explains why the fit is so loose around the line. On the original 2013 Dacoinminster power law, the 2017 top ran to 9.4x the curve and the 2018 low ended up below it. A model that misses by that much in both directions is tracing the trend through the noise, not measuring the forces that produce it.

Separate the two and the question shifts: if the underlying source of value keeps compounding while price doesn't, which of the two curves is the one that's wrong?

2124856506793300195.author: cryptojack
2124856506793300195.context: @cryptojack (489.655 seguidores), en inglés: los mineros de BTC están operando a pérdida y la capitulación minera ha marcado cada gran piso de ciclo (con gráfico). Post de ~1,3 h con 41 likes, 11 respuestas y 7.411 vistas. Ángulo: economía minera y el subsidio que baja de 3,125 a 1,5625 BTC por bloque (~450 a ~225 BTC al día) en el próximo halving.
2124856506793300195.suggested_text:
Mining at a loss creates a very specific kind of seller. Miners pay for electricity and hardware in fiat, so when revenue drops below cost, the least efficient ones sell their reserves and eventually unplug machines. That selling isn't a view on price, it's survival, and once the weakest operators exit, difficulty adjusts down and the pressure on the rest eases.

The backdrop makes this tighter every cycle. The subsidy today is 3.125 BTC per block, roughly 450 BTC a day; at the next halving it drops to 1.5625, about 225 a day. Each cut pushes the marginal miner closer to the edge unless price or fees make up the difference.

Capitulation has lined up with bottoms before, but it's a process rather than a single day. What tends to matter more is who is still mining when it's over.

2124879026321797393.author: DjaniWhaleSkul
2124879026321797393.context: @DjaniWhaleSkul (9.619 seguidores, en inglés): recibió un email que dice que hardware wallets como BitBox exigirán KYC obligatorio en Suiza (citando DAC8/OCDE) o dejarán de funcionar; concluye que es phishing, que su email se filtró y menciona los ataques físicos a holders en Francia. Noticia/alerta fresca (~24 min), cuenta mediana, 3 respuestas: encaja con custodia y filtraciones de datos.
2124879026321797393.suggested_text:
You read it right: it's phishing. A hardware wallet has no account to suspend. The keys live on the device, signing happens offline, and no vendor or regulator can switch that off remotely. Any email saying your wallet "stops working" unless you complete KYC is describing something the device physically can't do.

The real risk is the one you pointed at: the purchase record. Ledger's 2020 e-commerce leak exposed names, phone numbers and home addresses of 270k+ customers, and the phishing and threats that followed never really stopped. The keys were never touched; the shipping database was the weak point.

Self-custody has two layers that rarely get discussed together: protecting the seed, and protecting the fact that you hold one at all. Most setups only solve the first.

Stacking those four makes sense because each one measures something different: STH cost basis shows where recent buyers are underwater, MVRV and its Z-score compare price with the market's aggregate on-chain cost, and SOPR tells you whether coins are actually being spent at a loss. "Longest" depends on what you measure: time spent below the prior high, or how deep the fall goes. History gives a wide range for both. That's the uncomfortable part of bear markets: the bottom and the recovery are two separate events. The low usually comes with forced selling and leverage getting flushed. So "it could end any moment" may well be right about the low. The clock that matters for most holders tends to start after it.

CoinJoin não apaga o rastro, mas quebra a heurística que a análise on-chain mais usa: a de que todas as entradas de uma transação pertencem ao mesmo dono. Para quem deixa $BTC em exchange, a lição é outra: o saldo na tela é um direito contra a custódia de alguém, protegido por chaves que você nunca viu. Escrevi sobre como montar uma custódia air-gapped por conta própria: https://x.com/ForecastQuant/status/2123585216740528526

The two timeframes even show up in different data. Price lives on flows, but adoption lives on-chain, and the two can move in opposite directions for a long time: over the last year $BTC fell about 32% and the network still added roughly 2.5M addresses holding a balance.

That's the quiet part of "adoption drives the upside": with a fixed 21M supply, it's not just how many people show up, but how many of them end up holding their coins instead of renting exposure through someone else.

2124933751721386239.author: Cointelegraph
2124933751721386239.context: @Cointelegraph (2.925.584 seguidores), en inglés, con imagen: «JUST IN: US DOJ files to recover over $1.1 billion in USDC stolen by North Korean hackers in the $6 billion Binance hack, with nearly $3 billion in crypto already frozen, seized or returned.» Post de ~55 min con 75 likes, 15 reposts, 32 respuestas y 23.334 vistas. Ángulo: lo que se recupera tras un hackeo depende de emisores que pueden congelar (USDC) y de exchanges; custodia propia = nadie congela, nadie recupera.
2124933751721386239.suggested_text:
Notice where the recovery actually comes from. Most of what gets "frozen, seized or returned" after a hack is stablecoins with an issuer that can blacklist addresses, plus exchanges that cooperate. USDC can be frozen because Circle controls the contract: the same switch that helps victims here can lock anyone else out tomorrow.

Coins sitting on an exchange are a claim on that exchange, and the wallets pooling everyone's funds are exactly what state-backed groups like North Korea's go after. Bitcoin in keys you control works the other way: nobody can freeze it on you, and nobody can claw it back for you either.

That trade-off is the whole custody question, and most people only think it through after a headline like this one.
